content.text:
Talking to myself as I go:

- The screen is black, which is hard on my eyes even with my glasses.
- At the top I see "כל המסלולים בכל החברות" and the button "קופת גמל להשקעה 143" is already lit up. Good, that's what I came for.
- There's an orange box: "נתוני הרשות לא עודכנו מאז ספטמבר 2026". So the numbers aren't new. I'll keep that in mind.
- The buttons in the second row: "עוקב מדדי מניות 11" is lit. מדד to me is the price index on the news, but the task says stock indices, so I'll take it. "עוקב מדד s&p 500" has English letters, so I'll leave it.
- Under the buttons it says the companies are sorted "מהגדולה לקטנה לפי הכסף". So the cheapest isn't at the top. I'll have to go through them one by one.
- I'm reading the fee next to each one, "דמי ניהול ... מההחיסכון":
  - הראל 0.56%
  - מור 0.67%
  - אנליסט 0.6%
  - מיטב 0.65%
  - אלטשולר שחם 0.56%
  - הפניקס 0.6%
  - מגדל 0.62%
- Second screen:
  - כלל 0.63%
  - מנורה 0.57%, plus 0.02% "מההפקדה"
  - אינפיניטי 0.65%, plus 0.02%
  - אילון "עוד לא דווח", so they haven't reported a fee.
- The lowest is 0.56%, and two of them have it: הראל and אלטשולר שחם, both with 0% from deposits. I know הראל, it's a big company.

**What I'd tell my son:**
Listen, I found it. The lowest fee is 0.56% a year, and it's the same at הראל and at אלטשולר שחם. Neither one takes anything from the money you put in. I'd lean towards הראל because I know the name. מנורה is close, at 0.57%. I'm fairly sure about this. But the page itself says its figures haven't been updated since September. And I don't really know what "עוקב מדדי מניות" is, so before I sign anything I'll ask you, or ask at the bank.

I looked at the heading, the orange warning, the buttons, and the fee number in each row. I didn't open the little arrows on the side or the "?" marks. I didn't try to read the coloured circles with "מניות 99%" and "מט"ח 98%". מט"ח, I don't know what it means here. I also don't understand "מסלול אחד מתוך 16", or why most rows say "פחות מ־3 שנים" where I expected a yield. In the row headings the text is small and pale grey, and so is the line at the bottom about returns, so I couldn't read them properly. The dark screen with all those numbers made me anxious. At first I thought the list was in order of fee, and I had to check all eleven.

input.answer: The lowest fee for a stock-index investment kupat gemel is 0.56% of savings (and 0% on deposits), shared by הראל and אלטשולר שחם; I'd lean to הראל because I know the name, but I'll check with my son or the bank first.
